newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen firmer at Tokyo noon after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen firmer at Tokyo noon after FOMC.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen futures were firmer at noon on Wednesday on short-covering by traders after the Federal Reserve's policy-making arm left short-term rates steady.
Weak Tokyo stocks also added to the bullish sentiment across the yield curve of the yen debt markets.

The main factor behind the weakness in stocks was selling of futures by foreign investors, who see a chance that Japanese exporters may revise down their earnings forecasts in view of the dollar's steep fall recently, which in turn could delay a credit tightening.
Many had been expecting the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to let the call rate rise above the current 0.5 percent as early as July.

However, the yen's steep rise has gradually changed the market view, and some traders believe the BOJ may not be able to raise rates so soon, unless the yen stops climbing against the dollar and other currencies.
The dollar was traded at around 114 yen at 0300 GMT, compared with the 56-month peak of 127.47 yen on May 1.
The BOJ refrained from its regular market operations at 0020 GMT, leaving the market with a 10 billion yen shortfall.
